_: Little Big Questions, fossil pilot, SILENT STORY (Sam 23 Oct 20:09: no narration; music and sound design carry the story; sparse big words where needed; the picture explains). One fixed Fable view of one Cutaway block, no cuts, barely any camera movement. This beat sheet is the film's source of truth for picture, words, sound and music; facts in docs/research/KIDS_FACTS_2026-10.md 1.1. Times in seconds, 65 s total, timed to the music edit.

beats.name: hook
beats.picture: Today, a sunny meadow on top of the block; inside the rock below, the dark shape of a big bone, glinting once. The mascot peeks at it. A red ball rolls in from the edge and stops on the grass.
beats.words: HOW DO BONES TURN TO STONE?
beats.sound: meadow birds, a soft breeze, the ball's little bounce
beats.music: first flute phrase, the dawn theme alone (recording 0:00)

beats.name: rewind
beats.picture: Time runs backwards: the sky flickers through days and seasons in reverse, the layers above the bone pull away upward, the meadow melts into a fern forest and a river.
beats.sound: a reversed whoosh, a rising shimmer

beats.name: the living world
beats.picture: A big, gentle long-necked dinosaur munches ferns by the river; two small babies splash; dragonflies; a pterosaur glides; far away a herd walks the horizon and a volcano smokes. Easter eggs: a rubber-duck-yellow flower floating like a duck, the mascot riding a turtle.
beats.sound: river, munching (crunchy leaves), gentle heavy footsteps that make the ferns bounce, baby splashes, a far soft call
beats.music: the theme passes between flute and oboe, rising through new keys (0:10 to 0:21)

beats.name: the old dinosaur rests
beats.picture: Years pass in a breath: the big dinosaur, old now, walks slowly to the river bank, lies down, and stays still. The light softens to evening gold, one leaf drifts down. Nothing frightening: no wound, no predators, the babies have grown and walk off with the herd.
beats.sound: the world goes hushed: the river quieter, one bird, a long soft exhale of wind
beats.music: the softest moment, a turn to C major (0:21 to 0:25)

beats.name: mud covers the bones
beats.picture: Rain and a gentle flood: the river spreads brown mud and sand over the body; what remains is the skeleton, then the mud covers it like a blanket.
beats.sound: rain beginning, water rushing, wet squelches as each mud wave settles
beats.music: a swell at 0:26 as the flood spreads, then it settles

beats.name: layer on layer
beats.picture: Layer after layer stacks on top, each a different colour, each landing on a beat. Above ground the world races through eras: forests, ice, mammoths crossing, grasslands. The bones sink deeper in the cut-away view.
beats.sound: each layer lands with a soft thud; wind, snow, a far mammoth trumpet, grass rustle racing by
beats.music: quiet restart, the build begins at 0:35.5; each layer lands on a phrase pulse

beats.name: bone to stone
beats.picture: A round magnifier window opens on the bone inside the rock: tiny water drops seep in, each leaves a sparkle of crystal; the bone's colour slowly changes from ivory to stone grey with mineral glints, from one end to the other.
beats.sound: slow drips in a cave-like hush, tiny crystal tinkles
beats.music: a held, glowing passage; the stone hit at 43.0 on the phrase lift

beats.name: the land wears away
beats.picture: Wind and rain wear the top layers away, little by little; the hills shrink; the bone rises closer to the surface.
beats.sound: wind gusts, rain, small grit trickles

beats.name: the find
beats.picture: Today: a sunny morning, a girl with a hat and a little brush (her dog chasing a stick nearby), kneeling at a rock face on the side of the block. Brush, brush: the bone shape appears out of the rock. She jumps with joy.
beats.sound: brush scrapes in rhythm, the dog's happy bark, a tiny gasp-free 'ta-da' sparkle
beats.music: brush strokes on the climb; FOSSIL! on the full-orchestra sunrise climax at 49.5

beats.name: the send-off
beats.picture: The girl holds up her toy dinosaur next to the real fossil; the mascot waves from the meadow; the red ball from the start rolls back into view. The block settles into its gentle living loop.
beats.sound: meadow birds return, the ball bounce
beats.music: cross-fade at 53.0 to 54.5 into the piece's own ending (recording 3:37 to 3:49): one last swell (film 57 to 60) as she holds up the toy dinosaur, then the final quiet chord under WHAT IS UNDER YOUR FEET?

words_rules: Set in code (Fable lettering, large, readable on a phone, 2.5 s minimum on screen); no em dash, en dash or three dots; never drawn by a model.
sound_rules: Music is the voice of the film: foreground, not a bed (about -16 LUFS integrated, the voice slot is gone). Every event the picture shows has a sound; sound effects real CC0 recordings from the sfx-bank where they exist, playful synthesised accents (sparkles, thumps, rewind) from the score engine where they do not. Nothing harsh, sudden or scary: soft attacks, no loud stingers, true peak under -1.5 dBTP.

music.piece: Grieg, Peer Gynt Suite No. 1, I. Morning Mood
music.edit: recording 0:00 to 0:54.5, triangular cross-fade 1.5 s into 3:37.0 to 3:49.0; loudnorm -16 LUFS, true peak -1.5 dBTP; 65.0 s
